This is the way.|[[Din Djarin]] to [[Din Grogu]]|}} '''''Star Wars: The Mandalorian and Grogu''''', marketed and titled on-screen as '''''The Mandalorian and Grogu''''', is a live-action ''[[Star Wars]]'' film, released in theaters on [[May 22]], [[2026]]. The film, directed by [[Jon Favreau]], written by Favreau, [[Dave Filoni]], and [[Noah Kloor]], and produced by Favreau, [[Kathleen Kennedy]], Filoni, and [[Ian Bryce]], takes place between the events of [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Episode VI: Return of the Jedi'']] and [[Star Wars: Episode VII The Force Awakens|''Episode VII: The Force Awakens'']]. It continues and is a spinoff of the [[Disney+]] series [[Star Wars: The Mandalorian|''The Mandalorian'']]. In ''The Mandalorian and Grogu'', the characters of [[Din Djarin]] (the titular "[[Mandalorian]]") and [[Din Grogu|Grogu]] embark on a new adventure. The film stars [[Pedro Pascal]], reprising his role as Din Djarin, and [[Sigourney Weaver]]. [[Ludwig Göransson]], the original composer of ''The Mandalorian'', returns to score the film. The film is the first in a new slate of ''Star Wars'' films and takes place in the same timeline as the ongoing Disney+ series ''The Mandalorian'', a [[The Mandalorian Season Four|fourth season]] of which is still in development, and ''[[Star Wars: Ahsoka]]''. ''The Mandalorian and Grogu'' is the first live-action, cinematic-release ''Star Wars'' film to not include the "[[Opening crawl#Description|A long time ago in a galaxy far, far away]]" card, and the first to include opening credits. ==Opening crawl== {{OpeningCrawl |name=Star Wars: The Mandalorian and Grogu |text=The evil GALACTIC EMPIRE has fallen. Ex-Imperial Warlords remain scattered throughout the galaxy, plotting the Empire’s return. The fledgling NEW REPUBLIC has begun to reunite the galaxy. In the Lawless Outer Rim, THE MANDALORIAN and his young apprentice GROGU work to hunt down these Imperial fugitives.... }} ==Plot summary== ===Eliminating Barro=== [[Warlord|Imperial Warlord]] [[Commander]] [[Barro]] is convening a summit with several local leaders at a [[Phostera Imperial base|mountainous base]] on the [[Temperature|frigid]] [[planet]] of [[Phostera]] in the [[Outer Rim Territories]]. While promising protection, he raises their protection money. When one of the leaders, [[Prefect]] [[Nobah]], objects, Barro shoots him dead. The [[Mandalorian]] [[Din Djarin]] [[Attack on Barro's Imperial remnant|infiltrates]] the base and takes out several [[Cold weather assault trooper|snowtroopers]]. In the face of danger, Barro orders his snowtroopers and the local leaders to make a last stand while he flees in a [[turbolift]]. The Mandalorian enters the conference room and takes out the snowtrooper sentries. The leaders promptly surrender and point the way to the turbolift. Outside, [[Din Grogu]] uses [[the Force]] to disassemble a [[polar mouse droid]]. He then distracts an [[Unidentified Imperial Remnant AT-RT Driver|AT-RT Driver]] riding an [[All Terrain Reconnaissance Transport]] (AT-RT walker) long enough for Djarin to steal the walker and blast the [[Imperial Remnant AT-RT Driver|driver]]. Pursuing Barro, Djarin and Grogu take the AR-RT walker down the mountain. Barro flees in a convoy of three [[All Terrain Armored Transport]] (AT-AT walkers). The second walker's [[Vehicle commander|commander]], [[Fremmet]], manages to crush the stolen AT-RT walker with his vehicle's front legs. However, Djarin and Grogu escape with a [[jetpack]]. Djarin plants a set of [[grav charge]] explosives on the [[Walker Three|third AT-AT walker]], causing it to fall into a ravine and explode. The Mandalorian and Grogu then manage to enter Fremmet’s AT-AT walker through its rear compartment. He takes out the snowtroopers and one of the [[AT-AT pilot]]s before Fremmet seals himself and the remaining pilot inside the cockpit. Fremmet calls Barro for help and the Imperial warlord orders his two AT-AT pilots to climb onto the head of the first walker to shoot at Djarin. The Mandalorian blows up the head of Fremmet's walker with explosives, killing Fremmet and the remaining AT-AT driver, escaping to the lead walker. Barro orders the pilots of his walker to the roof to battle the Mandalorian; after taking out the two pilots, he and Grogu enter the front walker's cockpit through the head. However, Barro activates the [[autopilot]] and several explosives and flees aboard an [[INT-4 Interceptor]] inside his walker. Before the walker explodes, Djarin uses its [[Laser cannon|laser cannons]] to shoot down Barro's vehicle, killing him. Djarin and Grogu fly towards an orbiting [[UT-60D U-wing starfighter/support craft|U-Wing]] piloted by [[Garazeb Orrelios]], who reminds he was supposed to bring in the bad guy alive so they could point them to the other bad guys. Djarin apologizes for not completing his objective. The U-Wing then jumps to [[hyperspace]]. ===Working for the New Republic=== Djarin travels with Grogu to [[Adelphi Base]] where he meets with [[Colonel]] [[Ward]], who commands [[New Republic]] [[starfighter]] forces on [[Adelphi]]. Djarin now works as an independent contractor hunting Imperial war criminals for the New Republic. Ward is unhappy that Djarin did not capture Barro alive since she had hope that he would lead them to other Imperial fugitives. Ward explains that [[New Republic Intelligence]] has cultivated a relationship with two [[Hutt]] crime lords known as [[The Twins]]. In return for providing intelligence about Imperial fugitives including the elusive [[Janu Coin|Coin]], The Twins have sought the New Republic's help in retrieving someone. Given his past dealings with underworld elements, Colonel Ward believes that Djarin is best suited for this mission. As an advance payment, she entices him with a newly-refurbished [[ST-70 M-111 Razor Crest series|ST-70 assault ship]] as a replacement for his destroyed starship ''[[Razor Crest]]''. After inspecting the ''[[Razor Crest 2.0]]'' with Grogu, Djarin reluctantly accepts the mission and travels with the New Republic soldier and [[Alliance to Restore the Republic|Rebel Alliance]] veteran Garazeb Orrelios to [[Nal Hutta]], the homeworld of the Hutts. ===Hutt entanglements=== Djarin and his companions take the ''Razor Crest 2.0'' into hyperspace. Upon exiting hyperspace, they enter Nal Hutta's atmosphere. While approaching the [[Hutt Palace]], they are intercepted by a pair of [[HH-87 Starhopper]] (Hutt fighters) flown by members of the [[Droid Gotra]], a group of [[battle droid]] veterans of the [[Clone Wars]] serving as mercenaries for the [[Hutt Clan]] [[gangster]]s. Orrelios stays aboard the ship while Djarin and Grogu enter the Hutt Palace. After passing by several Hutts, they enter the Twins' throne room, which is guarded by two hulking [[security droid]]s. Inside, the [[Unidentified Hutt brother|Hutt brother]] and the [[Unidentified Hutt sister|Hutt sister]] brief Djarin about the mission. They task him with rescuing the late [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure]]'s surviving son, [[Rotta]], who has purportedly fallen with "bad company" on the moon [[Shakari]]. In return for a lucrative bounty and seeking to honor his relationship with the New Republic, Djarin accepts the [[Mission to Shakari|mission]] and travels with Grogu and Orrelios to Shakari. ===Seeking Rotta and Janu=== Arriving on the urban moon, Djarin and Grogu seek out Rotta while Orrelios waits aboard the ''Razor Crest 2.0''. While walking through the street markets, Djarin chats with an [[Ardennian]] [[fry cook]] named [[Hugo Durant]]. After Djarin gives him several [[Galactic Credit Standard|New Republic credit]]s, Durant reveals that Rotta has become a popular gladiator at [[The Pits (arena)|The Pits]] arena. Djarin and Grogu travel to The Pits where they find Rotta defeating a [[human]] gladiator to the cheers of the crowd. The duo later visit Rotta's quarters where Djarin tells him that his aunt and uncle, the Twins, have sent him to rescue him. Rotta, who is desperate to step out of his crime lord father's shadow, refuses because his master Janu has promised him his freedom after his last fight tomorrow night. Rotta reveals that The Twins want to kill him because he is Jabba's heir so that they can control the late [[Jabba's criminal empire]]. Despite his cold reception towards Djarin, Rotta thinks Grogu is cute and gets the Mandalorian's permission to feed him. Djarin returns to Hugo and seeks information about Janu. Fearing harm to his twelve children, Hugo reluctantly reveals that Janu is a crime lord who controls the moons of Shakari and extracts tributes from vendors like him. He tells Djarin that Janu has a drop-off zone at the [[Salt Bar]], a [[cantina]] below [[Korvin Station]]. After Grogu eats some fry snacks, Djarin leaves Hugo with some more coins. At the Salt Bar, Djarin seeks out Janu but is rebuffed by an [[Iktotchi]] named [[Hogsbreth]], who warns him to leave him. When Djarin refuses, Hogsbreth orders his henchmen to rough up the Mandalorian. The Mandalorian fights and takes out several of the henchmen while Grogu hides on a cage housing an avian creature. During the fight, Djarin breaks Hogsbreth's right horn. Janu then appears and orders an end to the hostilities. Janu invites Djarin and Grogu inside his office. When Djarin tells him that he has come to buy Rotta's freedom, Janu refuses and reveals that he intends to kill the Hutt gladiator during his last fight by releasing several [[Dejarik]] creatures. Janu attempts to bribe the Mandalorian by giving him a salt crystal, telling him that it is a fortune on Shakari. Djarin refuses and pours the salt crystal into Hogsbreth's alcoholic beverage. ===The gladiatorial fight and pursuit=== Djarin returns with Grogu to Rotta's quarters at the arena. He warns the Hutt about Janu's treachery but the Hutt refuses to believe him and summons security. The Mandalorian and Grogu are incapacitated by a sleeping gas. Later, the Mandalorian wakes up in a pen leading to the arena. Outside, Janu and Hogsbreth preside over the fight while Grogu is kept inside a cage. The crowd cheers as Janu announces that Rotta will be fighting against a rare Mandalorian specimen. Djarin attempts to reason with Rotta but the Hutt is determined to fight him in order to impress the crowd. Djarin grabs a sword to defend himself and manages to defeat Rotta without wounding him. When Janu and the crowd motion for him to kill Rotta, the Mandalorian refuses and tells them that Rotta has bought his freedom. Janu responds by announcing that he has freed Rotta to die and activates machinery releasing several Dejarik creatures, including a [[Ghhhk]], a [[Houjix]], a [[Kintan strider]], a [[K'lor'slug]], a [[Mantellian Savrip]] [[Unidentified Mantellian Savrip gladiator|gladiator]], a [[Monnok]] [[Unidentified Monnok gladiator|gladiator]], a [[Molator]], and an [[Ng'ok]]. As the creatures converge on the two, Djarin convinces Rotta to join forces to fight off the creatures and survive. The two use their melee weapons and physical strength to fight off the creatures. During the skirmish, Rotta throws the Houjix against one of the energy field generators that keeps the fighters and creatures confined to the arena. The creatures break free of the arena and begin attacking the spectators, devouring and maiming several people. Janu and Hogsbreth take the opportunity to flee. Djarin rescues Grogu from his cage. They join Rotta on the streets while the freed creatures wreak havoc. The K'lor'slug breaks into a monorail train above. After one of the creatures drives away a driver, Rotta steals a [[speeder]] and escapes, determined not to return to his uncle and aunt. After Djarin and Grogu save a [[Rodian]] mother and her child from being mauled, they pursue Rotta on a jetpack and [[hover pram]]. Following a speeder chase, they corner Rotta with the help of Orrelios, who is flying the ''Razor Crest II''. ===Capturing Commander Coin=== Intending to deliver him to the Twins, Djarin has Rotta restrained on a harness inside the cargo hold of the ''Razor Crest II''. Before the hyperspace jump, Djarin offers to release Rotta from his harness if he doesn't cause trouble. Rotta tells him and Orrelios that the Twins only want him back so that they can kill him and take over the Hutt Cartel. When Djarin tells him that the Twins had offered to reveal the identity of the elusive Imperial fugitive Commander Coin, Rotta reveals that the crime lord Janu and Coin are the same person. He mentions that Janu once took him to his [[Janu Coin's estate|beachside estate]] on Shakari, which had a lot of [[Stormtrooper|stormtroopers]]. With Orrelios's support, Djarin agrees to investigate this lead. Parking their starship on the beach, the trio confirm the presence of stormtroopers guarding Coin's estate. While Rotta waits aboard the ship with Grogu, Djarin and Orrelios attack the compound, seeking to capture Coin. Inside the living room, Coin briefs several stormtroopers and Hogsbreth about enforcement operations in the [[Shakari system]]. While Orrelios fights with other stormtroopers in the corridors, Djarin storms the living room and fights the stormtroopers and Hogsbreth, taking them out after a brief gun battle and melee. He also kills Hogsbreth with a [[flamethrower]]. Following a struggle, Djarin also captures Commander Coin. He and Orrelios escape with their captive in a stolen [[landspeeder]]. Stormtroopers give chase into landspeeders over the beach dunes. With their pursuers closing in on them, Djarin uses his [[comlink]] to radio Grogu and Rotta. With Rotta unable to fit inside the cockpit due to his Hutt physiology, Grogu attempts to prepare the ship for takeoff under Djarin's instruction. However, the child accidentally fires the ship's missile system twice, taking out one of the Imperial landspeeders and narrowly missing Djarin's landspeeder. Djarin and Orrelios board the ''Razor Crest 2.0'' but the second group of stormtroopers manage to drive their landspeeder up the ramp. While Djarin takes control of the cockpit and flies the ship, Orrelios and Rotta fight with the stormtroopers and manages to push them and their vehicle off into the dunes. Coin's neo-Imperial forces deploy three [[Shakari Gangster Fighter]]s after the ''Razor Crest 2.0'', leading to a chase in the skies of Shakari. To gain speed, Djarin gets Orrelios to rip up the motherboard, allowing him to bypass controls and turn the tables on their pursuers. Djarin shoots down two of the enemy starfighters and pursues the third into space. After shooting down the third starfighter, Djarin takes the ''Razor Crest 2.0'' into hyperspace. ===A change of plans=== Djarin and his companions return to Adelphi Base. While Rotta waits aboard the ''Razor Crest 2.0'', Djarin and Grogu deliver the fugitive Janus Coin to Colonel Ward at ''[[The Pilots' Rest]]''. Besides Ward, several New Republic pilots and officers including [[Trapper Wolf]], [[Carson Teva]], [[Blick]], [[Sash Ketter]], [[Dok Suri]], and [[Jib Dodger]] are also present at the cantina. Djarin tells Ward that he was unable to capture Rotta but has instead captured the elusive Commander Coin. He tells her that Coin has valuable information for the New Republic. Ward is disappointed that Djarin did not honor their agreement with the Hutt Twins but agrees to pay Djarin the reward money for Coin. Coin also requests a lawyer before being led away by two [[New Republic soldier]]s. Ward warns the Mandalorian that the Hutts will not take kindly to Djarin not delivering Rotta to them and adds that it would complicate the New Republic's relationship with the Hutts. Orrelios parts company with Djarin and rejoins his New Republic comrades. Djarin, Grogu and Rotta travel on the ''Razor Crest 2.0'' back to the [[Clan Mudhorn homestead]] on the outskirts of [[Nevarro City]]. The Mandalorian hires the [[Anzellan Droidsmiths]] [[Minch]], [[Keeto]], [[Bai]] and the newcomer [[Clang]] to modify his new starship to fit his specifications. He warns Grogu to "play nice" with the diminutive droidsmiths, who have developed a rapport with the youngling. Later, Djarin arranges for a droid [[smuggler|gunrunner]] to ferry Rotta into hiding aboard a [[TR-TL3 Terrapin-class bulk tanker|Turtle Tanker]]. ===Kidnapped by Embo=== Later in the night, the [[Kyuzo]] bounty hunter [[Embo]] travels aboard his saucer-shaped starship [[Guillotine (starship)|''Guillotine'']] to Nevarro, intent on delivering Djarin to the Hutt Twins for not honoring his promise to deliver Rotta to them. He scouts out the perimeter around the Clan Mudhorn homestead with his new pet [[Anooba]] and companion [[Keibu]]. The raid takes place on a rainy night. Djarin's two [[blurrg]]s sense a stranger approaching and alert Djarin. In response, Djarin tells Grogu and the Anzellan Droidsmiths to hide under a trapdoor while he covers the windows with retractable metal sheets and locks the front door. Embo attempts to surprise the Mandalorian by breaching a hole in the roof. However, the Mandalorian is able to track his heat signature using his helmet and detonates a [[grav charge]], causing Embo to fall through the ceiling. Djarin also signals for Grogu and the Anzellan Droidsmiths to retreat through a hatch outside the cabin. During the ensuing struggle, Embo manages to temporarily blind Djarin with a [[flash grenade]] before fleeing outside the cabin. However, this was a ruse for Keibu to sweep in and capture Grogu. Despite his efforts, the youngling managed to escape with three of the Anzellan Droidsmiths. Keibu instead captured the Anzellan leader Minch with her jaws. Following another struggle, Embo manages to capture the Mandalorian in a [[stun net]], shocking him unconscious. Having captured his target, Embo contacted his Hutt employers via [[holoprojector]] on his arm. The Twins ordered him to bring Djarin to their palace on Nal Hutta. After summoning the ''Guillotine'', Embo and Keibu depart with the incapacitated Djarin and Minch. Later, Grogu and the other Anzellans emerge from hiding and resolve to rescue the Mandalorian and Minch. They travel to Nal Hutta on their diminutive [[Anzellan Starship]]. Later, Djarin wakes up in a holding cell aboard the ''Guillotine''. He finds Keibu toying with Minch and manages to entice the Anooba into releasing the [[droidsmith]] with one of Grogu's sweets. Minch shelters with Djarin inside his cell before Keibu realizes the trick and pursues him. Hearing movement, Embo exits the cockpit and descends down into the holding cell. Djarin asked who had hired him, but before he could finish speaking, Embo shocks him unconscious. ===The pool of death and rescue=== Later, Embo arrives at the Hutt Palace and delivers Djarin to the Hutt Twins. Meanwhile, Minch takes the opportunity to escape the ''Guillotine'' and flee into the swampy forests of Nal Hutta. The Twins have already captured Rotta and bound him to an electric torture device, intending to torture him for centuries. The Hutt crime lords chastise Djarin for breaking his contract and reveal their intentions to punish him. To shame the Mandalorian, they remove his helmet. Djarin responds that he will kill them to ensure that no outsiders who see his face will survive. One of the Hutt twins tosses the helmet down a trapdoor that leads to a subterranean pool. Djarin himself is thrown into the watery pool while the Hutts gloat over his death sentence, intending to harvest his [[beskar]] armor once he has died and sell it on the [[black market]]. The Mandalorian is attacked by four amphibious [[Amani]] gladiators but he manages to kill them following a fierce struggle. The Hutts then unleash a large [[Hutt's dragonsnake|dragonsnake]] which inhabits the pool. Djarin regains his helmet and takes a spear from one of the dead Amani warriors. At the same time, Grogu and the other Anzellans land on Nal Hutta in their starship. After reuniting with Minch, they head to the Hutt Palace via an underground tunnel and reach a grated opening leading to the pool, where they witness Djarin fighting the dragonsnake. During the struggle, the dragonsnake managed to bite Djarin in the chest, with one of the Hutt Twins taunting him about dying from the creature's poison. Before the dragonsnake could devour Djarin, the Anzellans and Grogu used a grav charge to blow a hole in the pool, allowing Djarin to escape. Djarin manages to escape the Hutt Palace with his rescuers. In response, the furious Twins deploy several Droid Gotra sentry droids and Amani warriors after the fugitive Mandalorian. Djarin and his rescuers reach the parked Anzellan Starship in a forest clearing. Unable to board the diminutive starship due to his size, the seriously wounded Djarin told Grogu to flee with the Anzellan Droidsmiths, promising that he would join them. After they had departed, Djarin made a last stand against several pursuing droids and Amani warriors, before collapsing due to the effects of the dragonsnake poison. ===The kindly fisherman=== Disobeying Djarin's orders to flee, Grogu later resurfaced and tended to his mortally wounded father figure. With Djarin comatose and unresponsive due to the dragonsnake bite, Grogu used the Force to push him inside a hollow log to protect him from the elements. As dusk falls, Grogu becomes hungry and searches for food. He stumbles upon a riverside [[Gatori's hut|hut]] inhabited by a reptilian alien named [[Gatori]], who is sitting on a rocking chair. There are four fish being smoked on a nearby smoking rack. With Gatori seemingly asleep on his rocking chair, the hungry Grogu stole one of the fish and retreated to a tree trunk near Djarin's log where he ate his dinner. Still hungry, Gatori returned to Gatori's hut for seconds. Since the alien fisherman was still seemingly dozing on his rocking chair, Grogu approach the fishing rack from the riverbank. Before he could take another fish, the youngling was swallowed by a [[Unidentified Nal Hutta frog|large frog-like creature]]. Gatori then emerged from his supposed slumber and shot at the frog with his [[slingshot]], causing it to spit Grogu out and flee. Taking pity on the youngling, Gatori summoned Grogu to his hut and gave him another fish to eat. Sensing that Grogu had escaped from the Hutts, he warned the youngling about the danger posed by the crime lords. Due to his relative young age, Grogu was unable to speak but communicated through facial and bodily gestures. Shortly later, Embo and his Anooba Keibu approached Gatori, having been sent by the Hutt Twins to hunt down the fugitive Mandalorian. Gatori motioned for Grogu to hide with his fish behind some crates containing fish. While Embo chatted with the alien fisherman, Keibu began sniffing around the fish crates. Before she could sense Grogu, Gatori shouted at her to get away from the fish, saving Grogu from being captured. Embo and Keibu then left to resume their search for Djarin. After the visitors had left, Grogu emerged from hiding and Gatori revealed that Embo had told him about the Mandalorian's potentially deadly dragonsnake bite. Recognizing that Grogu was Djarin's adopted son, the alien fisherman took pity on Grogu and mixed several [[Plant|herb]] plants into an [[antidote]] for the [[poison]]. He warned Grogu that it might be too late to save his father and told the youngling to hurry. ===The return of the Mandalorian=== Heeding Gatori's advice, Grogu brought the herb concoction back to Djarin and feeds it to him. Overnight, the Mandalorian recovers and regains his strength. By morning, Djarin has fully recovered. He thanks Grogu for looking out for him, saying that the young care for the old. Reasoning that the Hutt Twins will continue to hunt him down if they are not stopped, Djarin decides to confront them and rescue Rotta. He and Grogu stumble upon the damaged Turtle Tanker, which had been ferrying Rotta, in the nearby forest. Djarin deduces that the ship was shot down by Starhopper Hutt starfighters and crash-landed. While exploring the cockpit, they find the incapacitated droid pilot. Three Amani warriors, who were sent by the Hutt Twins, corner the duo but the Mandalorian fights back and kills them. While rummaging through the damaged ship, Djarin finds an [[Amban phase-pulse blaster]] and two [[machete]]s on shelves with more weapons like [[vibroblade]]s and blaster packs. He discovers the Turtle Tanker is still airworthy and flies it towards the Hutt Palace. ===Rescuing Rotta=== Breaching through the palace's anti-air defenses, Djarin crash-lands the starship inside the building. He fights his way past the Droid Gotra sentry droids into the throne room. Arriving at the throne room, Djarin has Grogu release Rotta from his torture rack. He attempts to kill the Hutts Twins with his new Amban phase-pulse blaster but Keibu stops him and he ends up fighting Embo. The two hunters duel as Grogu tries to wake Rotta up. Rotta's uncle attempts to eat Grogu but Rotta intervenes and battles both of the Hutt Twins. As Rotta and Djarin battle their respective foes, Grogu is confronted by Keibu but he uses the Force to calm her down. Despite her initial resistance, Keibu calms down and allows Grogu to pet her. Seeing Rotta battling the Hutt Twins, Djarin notices the trapdoor is about to break. He evades Embo and stuns him with his new Amban rifle, which instantly agitates Keibu and causes her to run to her master's side. As Rotta continues to beat the Twins, his aunt warns that he is going to break the trapdoor. However the warning comes too late and everyone falls in. Grogu uses the Force to save Rotta by levitating him to safety. The Twins are left at the mercy of their dragonsnake and beg Embo to help them. However, Embo decides to leave with Keibu in the tunnel that Grogu and the Anzellans had made earlier. As the dragonsnake devours the Twins, the throne room gets breached by the remaining Droid Gotra guards. While Djarin holds them off with his Amban rifle, he gets a transmission from one of the Anzellan droidsmiths, who has returned with a squadron of [[Adelphi Rangers]] led by Colonel Ward. Having interrogated Janu, she learned that the Hutts were double-crossing the New Republic by feeding intelligence to the Imperial remnants. Despite Ward's reluctance, she orders her squad to fire at Djarin's location, where the Mandalorian reunites with Grogu and Rotta who encountered a dead end. Using his Amban rifle, Djarin blasts open a hole and the three jump into the moat below as the New Republic starfighters destroy the Hutt Twins' palace. ===Aftermath=== Returning to Adelphi, Djarin talks with Rotta, who has decided to stay and aid the New Republic. In turn, Rotta advises Djarin to continue to look out for Grogu. As they depart Adelphi in the ''Razor Crest'', Djarin gives Grogu permission to initiate the jump to hyperspace. ==Development== {{Quote|Dave Filoni and Jon Favreau have a new vision, continuing on with a Mandalorian movie.|Giancarlo Esposito|{{WebCite|url=https://www.cultureslate.com/editorials/dragon-con-qa-with-star-wars-guests-from-ahsoka-the-mandalorian-the-book-of-boba-fett-and-the-acolyte|text=Dragon Con Q&A With 'Star Wars' Guests From 'Ahsoka,' 'The Mandalorian,' 'The Book Of Boba Fett,' And 'The Acolyte’|author=Cate Feeney|date=2024-09-27|work=[https://www.cultureslate.com ''CultureSlate'']|archivedate=20241003035121}}}} ''The Mandalorian and Grogu'' was announced, originally as ''The Mandalorian & Grogu'', on [[January 9]], [[2024]] on [[StarWars.com]] with a conceptual sketch by veteran illustrator [[Ryan Church]], along with an announcement of a [[Ahsoka Season 2|second season]] of the television series ''[[Star Wars: Ahsoka]]''. It was reported that a [[The Mandalorian Season Four|fourth season of ''The Mandalorian'']] was still in development.{{WebCite|url=https://deadline.com/2024/01/mandalorian-grogu-movie-jon-favreau-lucasfilm-1235700326|text='The Mandalorian & Grogu': Jon Favreau To Direct And Produce 'Star Wars' Pic For Lucasfilm|author=Matt Grobar|date=2024-01-09|archivedate=20240109174536}} However, series actor [[Giancarlo Esposito]] suggested the film was part of "a new vision" for ''The Mandalorian''. As Favreau later told SFX Magazine: "You can't just take those scripts and turn them into a movie. There were a lot of characters, it assumed you'd watched the whole show, and it was teeing up what was happening moving into ''Ahsoka''. It was about [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo|Grand Admiral Thrawn]] and following the larger storyline. This is a completely different medium, so I had to start from scratch, essentially."{{WebCite|url=https://www.gamesradar.com/entertainment/star-wars-movies/the-original-mandalorian-season-4-scripts-helped-set-up-ahsoka-season-2-but-jon-favreau-had-to-start-from-scratch-for-the-mandalorian-and-grogu|text=The
